fullPassage: It's easy to romanticize the hunter-gatherer way of life as a Huckleberry Finn existence filled with adventure and hunting expeditions, lived in small, close-knit communities in an unspoiled world. But, in actual fact, there is much to suggest that our ancestors' lives were in many ways complete hell. The average life expectancy was around 30 years, which isn't to say that everyone would drop dead at 30, but that many died young. As many as half died before they reached their teens - normally during birth or of an infection. Those who did make it to adulthood lived with the imminent threat of starvation, blood loss, dehydration, animal attacks, even more infections, accidents, and murder. Only a fraction would have made it to today's retirement age and yes, there were hunter-gatherers who lived to be 70 or even 80. So old age in itself is nothing new, but the fact that so many people are now reaching it is. Around 10,000 years ago, probably the single most significant shift in our ancestors' way of life occurred: we became farmers. But spears and bows weren't replaced by plows overnight; this gradual transition from a nomadic to an agricultural lifestyle took place over the course of centuries. The farmers' living conditions can be summarized quite simply: an even greater hell. The average life expectancy of around 30 years and the ever-present threat of death remained unchanged, although perhaps with a lesser risk of starvation. Instead, murder became an increasingly common cause of death, presumably because improved means of storing food and harvesting resources meant there was more to fight over. Hierarchies became more pronounced, and on top of that, a number of contagious diseases appeared on the scene. Work tasks grew more monotonous and working hours longer. Diets became less varied, most likely consisting of cereals for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

The average life expectancy was around 30 years, which isn't to say that everyone would drop dead at 30, but that many died young. As many as half died before they reached their teens - normally during birth or of an infection. Those who did make it to adulthood lived with the __________ threat of starvation, blood loss, dehydration, animal attacks, even more infections, accidents, and murder. Only a fraction would have made it to today's retirement age and yes, there were hunter-gatherers who lived to be 70 or even 80. So old age in itself is nothing new, but the fact that so many people are now reaching it is. Around 10,000 years ago, probably the single most significant shift in our ancestors' way of life occurred: we became farmers. But spears and bows weren't replaced by plows overnight; this gradual transition from a nomadic to an agricultural lifestyle took place over the course of centuries. The farmers' living conditions can be summarized quite simply: an even greater hell. The average life expectancy of around 30 years and the ever-present threat of death remained unchanged, although perhaps with a lesser risk of starvation. Instead, murder became an increasingly common cause of death, presumably because improved means of storing food and harvesting resources meant there was more to fight over. Hierarchies became more pronounced, and on top of that, a number of contagious diseases appeared on the scene. Work tasks grew more monotonous and working hours longer. Diets became less varied, most likely consisting of cereals for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

✅ ③ imminent(임박한): 성인이 되어도 기아, 출혈, 탈수 등 '임박한' 위협 속에 살았다는 내용과 일치 ← 정답
❌ ④ occasional(간혹의): 평균 기대수명이 매우 짧았다는 전체 흐름과 어울리지 않는 가벼운 표현

(B) This diet plan didn't <u>work</u> for her at all.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 work가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: work: (A) (과제 등을) 하다, 작업하다 (B) 효과가 있다
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 작업하다 — (B) 효과가 있다: (A)는 '에세이를 작업할 시간이 없다' → 작업하다, (B)는 '식단이 전혀 효과가 없었다' → 효과가 있다 ← 정답
❌ ② (A) 효과가 있다 — (B) 작업하다: (A)는 '에세이 작업'이므로 효과가 있다는 뜻이 아님
❌ ③ (A) 작업하다 — (B) 작업하다: (B)는 식단이 '효과가 있었는지'를 말하는 것이지 작업의 의미가 아님
❌ ④ (A) 효과가 있다 — (B) 효과가 있다: (A)는 에세이 작업을 가리키므로 효과가 있다는 뜻이 아님
det.tip: work: ① 작업하다(일하다) ② 효과가 있다(효과를 내다) — 문맥으로 구분

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "moving from place to place rather than living in one location permanently"

❌ ① permanent(영구적인): 한 곳에 머무른다는 뜻으로 정의와 반대
❌ ② stationary(정지된): 움직이지 않는다는 뜻으로 정의와 반대
❌ ③ domestic(국내의, 가정의): 이동 여부와 관련 없는 단어
✅ ④ nomadic(유목의): 한 곳에 영구히 머물지 않고 이곳저곳 이동한다는 정의와 일치 ← 정답
det.tip: nomadic=유목의, 이동하며 사는(ant: settled, permanent)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 글 전체가 과거 수렵채집 사회와 농경 사회의 삶을 서술하는 과거시제이므로, 앞 문장의 became과 같은 시제를 맞춰 appear를 과거형 appeared로 바꿔야 한다. 'a number of contagious diseases appeared on the scene'에서 주어 diseases에 대한 동사가 필요.
det.tip: appear(동사: 나타나다) → appeared(과거형) — 글 전체가 과거시제로 서술됨

questions.passage: Around 10,000 years ago, probably the single most significant shift in our ancestors' way of life occurred: we became farmers. But spears and bows weren't __________ (replace) by plows overnight; this gradual transition from a nomadic to an agricultural lifestyle took place over the course of centuries.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 주어 spears and bows가 '대체하는' 주체가 아니라 '대체되는' 대상이므로 수동태가 필요하다. weren't 뒤에 '과거분사'가 와야 수동태(be + p.p.)가 완성되므로 replace를 과거분사 replaced로 바꿔야 한다. 'weren't replaced by plows'는 '쟁기로 대체되지 않았다'는 의미.
det.tip: replace(동사: 대체하다) → replaced(과거분사) — be동사(weren't) + p.p. = 수동태

❌ ④ far safer than before(이전보다 훨씬 안전한): 살인과 질병이 늘었다는 뒤 내용과 정반대
